meta.name: rust-dev
meta.description: Practical day-1 guide to building applications in Rust well. Covers the mental model (ownership, errors as values, traits-not-interfaces), day-1 decisions (String vs &str, Box vs Rc vs Arc, dyn vs impl Trait, anyhow vs thiserror), idioms to internalize early, anti-patterns to avoid, and a tight crate shortlist (tokio, serde, anyhow, clap, reqwest, tracing, axum, sqlx). Use when starting a new Rust project, learning Rust coming from Python/JS/Go/Java/C++, deciding on types and lifetimes, choosing crates, structuring modules, configuring Cargo.toml/clippy/rustfmt, writing tests, benchmarking, profiling, or speeding up builds, or whenever the user mentions Rust, cargo, ownership, borrow checker, lifetimes, traits, async Rust, testing, or "writing this in Rust".
